sample_unit: case scenario responses (44 fictional scenarios x 5 runs/clinicians)
models_evaluated: RAG-enhanced LLM grounded in EAU and AUA guidelines (with Charlson Comorbidity Index life expectancy module)

links.outcome: Guideline-concordant PSA testing recommendations by RAG-grounded LLM versus junior clinicians
links.effect: RAG-LLM concordant in 95.5% (210/220) of scenarios vs junior clinicians 62.3% (137/220) closed-book and 74.1% (163/220) open-book; both P<.001.
links.quote: The RAG-LLM tool provided guideline-concordant recommendations in 95.5% (210/220) of case scenarios, compared to junior clinicians, who were correct in 62.3% (137/220) of scenarios in a closed-book format and 74.1% (163/220) of scenarios in an open-book format.

links.outcome: Comparison of candidate AI against junior clinicians on the same scenarios
links.effect: RAG-LLM 95.5% accuracy vs junior clinicians 62.3% (closed-book) and 74.1% (open-book); differences significant (P<.001).
links.quote: The difference was statistically significant for both closed-book (P<.001) and open-book (P<.001) formats.

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates an LLM pipeline using RAG on clinical vignettes against junior clinicians, but does not compare performance with and without RAG/guardrails or test an organizational deployment practice.
